conclusion: The current ESP32-S3 USB Serial/JTAG data path has no documented/supported DMA or GDMA attachment or DMA-enable setting. The separate USB-OTG controller has its own internal DMA; this is not a feature switch of the current driver.

references.finding: Lists peripherals sharing GDMA: SPI2, SPI3, UHCI0, I2S0/1, LCD/CAM, AES, SHA, ADC, RMT; USB Serial/JTAG is absent.
GDMA peripheral selector values0..9 enumerate those devices;10..63 invalid. SDK gdma_channel.h lines11..21 matches.
USB Serial/JTAG is fixed CDC-ACM/JTAG hardware; full-speed12Mbps, up to64-byte endpoint payload; CDC registers exposed toCPU viaAPB.
Firmware writes bytes to EP1_REG while room exists and flushes; host periodically checks for queued data. No DMA interface/descriptors are specified.
USB-OTG has an internalDMA AHB master interface; it and USB Serial/JTAG share the internal PHY. Simultaneous separate ports require the other PHY path.
USB-OTG supports CPU Slave mode, BufferDMA and Scatter/GatherDMA. This hardware capability alone does not establish whether a particular TinyUSB device backend enables DMA.

actual_driver_path.finding: Bounded tx_mux take; xRingbufferSend at281 copies into BYTEBUF; enable IN_EMPTY interrupt; returns size on whole-item acceptance or0.
Copies input bytes with memcpy into ringbuffer, including wrap split.
On SERIAL_IN_EMPTY, takes up to64bytes from ringbuffer in ISR, calls LL FIFO writer and flush, returns ring item; supports bounded stash if not all bytes enteredFIFO.
CPU loop checks serial_in_ep_data_free and writes each byte to EP1.rdwr_byte.
Waits for driver idle semaphore; no DMA completion path. Driver drain observation is not application-level PC acknowledgement.

repository_binding.rx_reader_count_claim: Not re-audited in this narrow DMA task

performance_boundary: FIFO CPU copies and interrupts have a cost, but their CPU time was not measured here.
The documented12Mbps is signalling rate, not guaranteed PC payload throughput.
Previously recorded per-record vTaskDelay and bounded application queue rejection/expiry are separate mechanisms; DMA would not cancel application waits or make the host consume data.
SPI DMA in the ADS driver is unrelated to USB Serial/JTAG hardware support.

A future OTG implementation would need separate driver/stack, descriptors, PHY ownership, USB identity/reenumeration and boot/debug coexistence validation; none was implemented or claimed by this review.
